title: Geo-seismic: USGS quakes on the globe, IRIS seismo-acoustics in the bridge
shape: Point-process transducer (USGS) -> band claim -> residual router. The globe shows every event; nothing tests a rate.
flow: claim(band on rate or mag) ──▶ test() ──▶ residual ──▶ route()
IRIS FDSN ──obspy──▶ seismo_fetch ──▶ seismo_encoder   (bridge; not on the globe, heavy deps)

notes.bottleneck: The Hurricane folder's dependency stack (obspy, pandas, torch). The USGS path needs none of it; keep them apart.
notes.leverage: The claim loop is already calibrated on a Poisson clock (4.0% false alarm at α=0.05). A quake feed is the first real Poisson-ish transducer it would see.
notes.harmonics: Aftershock decay is structure in a residual; the NOISE_AS_SIGNAL branch was built for a periodic rider and its power against a power-law decay is unmeasured.
notes.tertiary: A regional rate claim that fires MISSING_VARIABLE on 'region' is a claim about USGS network coverage, not seismicity. Record the source network as a covariate.

gev.role: USGS all_day.geojson poll, M2.5+, depth bands <70/<300 km, static ellipse axes (measured 32.4 -> 1.4 ms/frame)
earthquakes: numeric [magnitude, depthKm], text [place]; spoken queries over the loaded records
layerFeedState(): the six-value feed state every layer reports through

bridge.role: IRIS FDSN fetch of ground displacement + infrasound (needs obspy)
reading()/claim()/route(): the band claim and the four-way residual fork, calibrated on a Poisson clock
RollingBaseline: EWMA + Welford, Pi-Zero-sized, no numpy
elastic_stress, hydrostatic_pressure: the physics helpers a depth band would Gray-code through

ecosystem.why: github/claim_playground is this package's claim registry; a quake-rate claim is a T1-T4 candidate
premise check before a rate claim is registered: what is the null (Poisson) and is the feed complete at M2.5
aftershock clustering is structure in the residual, which is the NOISE_AS_SIGNAL branch's domain

avenues.title: USGS feed as a transducer for the field claim loop
avenues.moves: each polled event -> reading(channel='usgs.m2.5', value=magnitude, covariates={depth_band, region}, t_s=epoch)
avenues.fails_if: route() reports NOISE_AS_SIGNAL on a synthetic Poisson event stream at more than the 4.0% false-alarm rate the loop was calibrated to; then the adapter, not the feed, is structured

avenues.title: Aftershock structure as the NOISE_AS_SIGNAL positive control
avenues.moves: an Omori-law synthetic (rate ~ 1/(t+c)^p) through slotted_scan(); a real mainshock day from the USGS feed as the field case
avenues.fails_if: the permutation null does not separate the Omori stream from the Poisson stream at n >= AUTOCORR_MIN_N; a detector with 100% power at period 6/12/24 s may still be blind to a power-law decay, and that has not been measured

avenues.title: Depth bands are a 2-bit non-Gray code
avenues.moves: depthColor() thresholds (70, 300 km) restated as Gray bands via abstract_encoder; nothing visible changes
avenues.fails_if: the bands are consumed by nothing but a colour picker, in which case the Gray rule buys nothing here and this avenue is decoration

interference: seismo_fetch.py imports obspy, requests, pandas, torch (via jepa_manifold): the Hurricane folder is the heaviest dependency surface in the repo and none of it is needed to consume USGS GeoJSON
GEV's quake magnitude is the USGS 'mag' field, mixed Mw/Ml/Md by network; a band claim on 'magnitude' is a claim on a projection and must name it (FCL-9)
